executive_summary.headline: Karpathy built a better YouTube feed in two hours, and Claude did the work
executive_summary.body: HackerTube distills 43M Hacker News comments into 6,454 recommended videos, built and deployed by Claude on Opus 5.5 at medium effort, with the data zip published for remixing. Pieter Levels had Claude Code cut a full 10-minute vlog the same weekend.

executive_summary.headline: GPT-6.1 Terra makes computer use fast and cheap
executive_summary.body: OpenAI says Terra matches GPT-6 Astra at one-tenth the cost on Agents' Last Exam, and Greg Brockman says it feels faster than doing the work himself. Cursor, GitHub Copilot and the OpenAI API picked it up within the week.

executive_summary.headline: Genie 4 turns world models into something you steer in real time
executive_summary.body: Google's interactive model adds native audio, physics and Gemini reasoning, and early posters are already running DOOM and a GTA Waymo scene inside it. Research preview now, Ultra and API access to follow.

executive_summary.headline: Science gets concrete numbers
executive_summary.body: Anthropic reports a document review cut from 25.9 hours to 2.8 at Enveda and a 20-institution AI for Science expansion, while NVIDIA shows agents steering a radio telescope in plain language.

executive_summary.headline: Personal agents gain a texting interface and open-weight options close in
executive_summary.body: ChatGPT's Dot now takes tasks by iMessage, Grok Bot adds Pages and gift buying, and Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Pika H3 Flex ship open weights you can run locally.

top_picks.title: Karpathy built HackerTube in about 2 hours with Claude: 6,454 videos distilled from 43M Hacker News comments
top_picks.author: Andrej Karpathy
top_picks.summary: Andrej Karpathy had Claude Code filter 20 years of Hacker News comments down to 6,454 videos that keep getting recommended, then deploy a no-login viewing site, in roughly 2 hours on Opus 5.5 at medium effort. The data behind it ships as a zip so anyone can point their own Claude at it and make a version.
key_takeaways: Claude did the data filtering, the code, and the server hardening and deploy; Karpathy did the API key, VPS and domain purchase in the browser.
Recs use no logins and keep state in the local browser session.
Underlying comment-analysis data is published as one zip for remixing.
suggested_actions: Open hackertube.org and pick tonight's watch from it.
Download the zip, give it to your agent, and ask for a version tuned to your own field.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: replace an algorithmic feed you dislike with your own, built from a community's comment history. Try it: take 20 years of comments from a forum your team reads (materials, building science, a trade subreddit) and have an agent surface the links and papers people keep recommending.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A weekend project with real daily utility, built end to end by talking to an agent.

top_picks.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra: fast, lower-priced computer use and sharper writing
top_picks.author: OpenAI
top_picks.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra reads what is on screen, acts across apps and writes more naturally, at a lower price than earlier Terra models. Greg Brockman says computer use with Terra "feels faster at using a computer than what I can do unassisted," and OpenAI says it matches GPT-6 Astra at one-tenth the cost on Agents' Last Exam.
key_takeaways: Fast computer use is the headline: the model understands the screen and takes action across apps.
OpenAI's own chart claims parity with Astra at one-tenth the cost on Agents' Last Exam.
Also coming to the API and Codex; live in GitHub Copilot the same day.
suggested_actions: Hand Terra a recurring desktop chore this week and time it against doing it yourself.
Swap it into an existing agent loop and compare cost per task.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: computer use is now fast enough to be a daily tool. Try it: pick the five-minute browser chore you repeat every week (pulling a report, filing a form) and let Terra do it while you watch the clock.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Cheap, fast computer use widens who can run desktop agents.

secondary_urls.label: Greg Brockman on Terra computer use
OpenAI Developers: Terra in API and Codex

top_picks.title: Sundar Pichai unveils Genie 4: a real-time interactive world model with native audio and physics
top_picks.author: Sundar Pichai
top_picks.summary: Genie 4 lets you steer dynamic environments in real time, with audio generated to match, photorealistic scenes and physics, and multi-step events reasoned through by Gemini. It starts as a research preview for trusted testers and comes to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and to the Gemini API and AI Studio soon.
key_takeaways: Environments respond to prompts mid-simulation, with sound and conversation from characters.
Rollout: trusted testers now, Ultra subscribers and API access to follow.
Early users are already posting a "GTA Waymo" scene and Genie 4 running DOOM.
suggested_actions: Join the Project Genie waitlist if you hold an Ultra plan.
Sketch one scene (a plant floor, a showroom, a wind tunnel) you would want to walk through.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a world you can talk to is a new prototyping surface. Try it: describe a space you are designing and steer through it to see what the first draft feels like before anyone builds a model.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Physics-aware, audio-enabled interactive worlds are a step past video generation.

secondary_urls.label: Justine Moore: GTA Waymo from Genie 4

top_picks.title: Anthropic details early drug-development results with six partners, including 89% faster document review at Enveda
top_picks.author: Anthropic
top_picks.summary: Anthropic reports results from six research partnerships plus its own programs. Examples from the post: about 35,000 antibody designs at Divergence with three IgE disruptors that appeared to outperform Xolair, 6 to 9 times tighter binding at BigHat in 10 weeks, and Enveda review of 1,061 pages in 2.8 hours versus 25.9 manually.
key_takeaways: Generate: a CAR T-cell signaling design about 70% shorter with roughly 10 times as many receptors on the cell surface.
BigHat: about 1,010 variants tested in 10 weeks; stability up 8 to 18 degrees C.
Mithril Medicine, acquired by Anthropic, roughly doubled grip strength in mice; human trials targeted as soon as late 2028.
suggested_actions: Read the post for how each partner structured the Claude workflow.
Pick one slow document-review step in your own R&D process and time a Claude pass against the manual hours.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: the Enveda result is a scientist-friendly proof point, 25.9 hours down to 2.8 on a real review. Try it: pick one review your researchers dread, run it through Claude alongside them, and show the hours saved at the next group meeting.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Concrete lab-side numbers from a primary source, the kind of evidence that persuades skeptical scientists.

secondary_urls.label: Anthropic: early progress in drug development

top_picks.title: ChatGPT lets you text your Dot over iMessage or RCS, with tasks, photos and voice notes
top_picks.author: ChatGPT
top_picks.summary: ChatGPT now lets Pro users in the US text their personal agent, the Dot, to hand off tasks or ask it to keep watch on something, and it texts back proactively with updates. It works with text, photos and voice notes, and rolls out now as a preview.
key_takeaways: Texting reaches the same context and plugins as the app.
Proactive updates mean the agent starts conversations when something changes.
Preview for US Pro users; usage limits for Pro tiers were doubled the next day.
suggested_actions: Text your Dot one thing to watch (a price, a flight, a shipping status) and see what it sends back.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: an agent you reach the way you reach a coworker, by text. Try it: text your Dot a photo of something you need figured out and ask it to follow up tomorrow.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Messaging is the easiest interface for non-technical people, and this puts a persistent agent inside it.
top_picks.recurrence_note: Personal agents (Duet, Grok Bot, Muse, Dots) were last week's lead theme; this week adds the texting interface.

top_picks.title: Pieter Levels had Claude Code with Opus 5.5 edit his full 10-minute vlog from raw DJI clips
top_picks.author: @levelsio
top_picks.summary: Pieter Levels dropped his DJI clips into a folder, opened Claude Code in it and asked for a 10-minute vlog. It transcribed his speech with mlx-whisper and cut the edit, and he says he made only a few adjustments. Greg Isenberg called it the moment anyone wanting to vlog or build a video marketing machine could do it without a team.
key_takeaways: Workflow: clips in a folder, Claude Code opened in it, a one-line request.
Transcription ran locally with mlx-whisper.
Levels reports a few manual tweaks, not a rebuild.
suggested_actions: Point your coding agent at a folder of phone clips from a site visit or demo and ask for a 3-minute cut.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a coding agent is a video editor if you give it a folder. Try it: record a quick walkthrough of a prototype or lab setup, and ask the agent to turn it into a captioned two-minute update.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A creator-grade edit with no editing skills.

secondary_urls.label: Greg Isenberg on Opus 5.5 and video

top_picks.title: AI agents now steer the Allen Telescope Array in its search for alien signals, in natural language
top_picks.author: NVIDIA AI
top_picks.summary: At the SETI Institute, agents calibrate and focus the Allen Telescope Array, clean incoming data, run models and plot results from natural-language requests. NVIDIA says the Holoscan pipeline handles 2.4 terabits per second, and that it produced the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar in the Crab Nebula.
key_takeaways: Natural-language requests drive calibration, focusing, data correction and plotting.
Inference runs on premises next to the instrument on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs.
NVIDIA says agents compress weeks or years of human work into hours.
suggested_actions: Ask your instrument vendor which of your lab tools expose a command interface an agent could drive.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: scientists operate instruments by talking to them. Try it: take one repetitive instrument setup routine (calibration, scan parameters) and have an agent draft the sequence from plain-English intent.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A vivid example of agents controlling physical scientific equipment.

secondary_urls.label: NVIDIA blog: Agentic AI joins the search for extraterrestrial signals

top_picks.title: Canva introduces Brush, a vision-language model that edits designs alongside you
top_picks.author: Canva
top_picks.summary: Brush sees a design's layout, layers and style, and edits with you: fix one line of text, restyle a whole deck or build from a blank page. The post drew 2.5 million views.
key_takeaways: First vision-language model built for design, per Canva.
Handles single edits through whole-deck restyles.
suggested_actions: Take your current slide deck and ask Brush to restyle it to a new brand look.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a design model that understands layers makes every deck a draft you can reshape in a sentence. Try it: restyle last quarter's review deck three ways in ten minutes and pick the winner.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Small teams get a design partner that edits, not just generates.

sections.title: Tool Announcements
sections.description: New models, products and features announced on X this week, ordered by priority.

items.title: Google introduces Gemini 4 Carbon, ranked #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
items.author: Google
items.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon ranks #1 on v5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and sets new marks in cybersecurity and long-horizon work. It rolls out first to cyber defenders through Google's Fairwind Program, with wider access coming. Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas says it is the strongest model his team has seen for long-form research and that it is coming to Perplexity Pro and Max in Computer.

secondary_urls.label: Artificial Analysis: Carbon #1 on Index v5

items.title: Claude removes the 5-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts, and Max plans are renamed Max and Ultra
items.author: Boris Cherny
items.summary: Boris Cherny announced the 5-hour usage limit is gone for verified Ultra accounts. Anthropic also renamed Max 5x to Max ($100 a month) and Max 20x to Ultra ($200), with prices unchanged.

items.title: OpenAI gives eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers up to $500 a month in API credits
items.author: OpenAI Developers
items.summary: Pro plans get $100, $200 or $500 a month by tier, and Business plans get credits per seat, to build apps and agents through the API. The post drew 2.1 million views.

items.title: Cursor releases its Agent SDK: define agents in Markdown and TypeScript, deploy hosted or self-run
items.author: Cursor
items.summary: The SDK lets you write agent prompts in Markdown and tools in TypeScript, deploy on Cursor's hosted infrastructure or your own, and use built-in evals to measure each change.

items.title: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk") ships open weights: 1.05T parameters, #1 open model from outside China per Artificial Analysis
items.author: Artificial Analysis
items.summary: Artificial Analysis scores Mistral Large 4 at 26 on its Intelligence Index v5, one point ahead of the leading US open-weights model. Mistral says it ranks #1 among open models on Cognition's FrontierCode.

items.title: Kimi launches 3D Make: connect to Blender and CAD tools to build models, scenes and games
items.author: Kimi.ai
items.summary: Kimi connects to Blender and CAD tools to create models, assemble scenes and develop games, available on kimi.ai and Kimi Work.

items.title: Pika H3 Flex debuts as the #1 open-weight text-to-video model, with 15-second clips and audio in as little as 7 seconds
items.author: Pika
items.summary: Pika says H3 Flex tops DesignArena's text-to-video board among open-weight models, with 4K output, exportable audio stems and faster-than-realtime generation.

items.title: Cursor design mode adds Annotate: draw on the page to give agents visual prompts
items.author: Cursor
items.summary: Annotate lets you edit elements, draw on the page and review designs at different screen sizes, so agents take visual instructions instead of only text.

items.title: Unsloth runs the 1-trillion-parameter Mistral Large 4 on a Mac Studio with 1-bit GGUF
items.author: Unsloth AI
items.summary: Unsloth's 1-bit GGUF keeps 91% top-1 accuracy, putting a 1T-parameter open model on a desktop Mac, with a guide and weights on Hugging Face.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash lands in Cursor at $0.60 to $0.98 per task on CursorBench
items.author: Cursor
items.summary: Cursor says every effort level of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash sits on its CursorBench cost frontier, with no model scoring higher at those prices.

secondary_urls.label: Unsloth GGUFs for V4.1 Flash, runs on 64GB+ RAM

items.title: Runway App Studio: describe a creative app and it builds one that uses Runway models and your Brand Kits
items.author: Runway
items.summary: No code required: App Studio generates images, video and audio apps from a description, for you or your whole team.

items.title: Gemini adds shareable avatars that star in images and videos with friends
items.author: Google Gemini
items.summary: You can create a personal avatar, share it, tag friends in prompts and keep character and voice consistent, with access you can revoke.

items.title: Google AI Studio adds XR Blocks: vibe code 3D apps with hand tracking and tabletop physics from a prompt
items.author: Google AI Studio
items.summary: Supports hand tracking and pinch gestures, tabletop and wall physics, and 360-degree 3D holograms from text or photos.

items.title: Nous Research opens the Hermes Agent mobile app for iOS and Android beta testing
items.author: AI News | TestingCatalog
items.summary: TestingCatalog reports the Hermes mobile beta is live on TestFlight and Android, bringing the open-source agent to phones.

items.title: Perplexity rolls out voice mode in Computer for Pro and Max on web and Mac
items.author: Aravind Srinivas
items.summary: Aravind Srinivas says you can talk to your computer to run parallel work streams.

items.title: Liquid AI's LFM3 arrives on Ollama: text model fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit with 256K context
items.author: ollama
items.summary: Small text, vision, audio, omni and decision models that run locally and fine-tune on a single GPU.

items.title: Gemini adds immersive explorations: interactive scenes for topics like jet engines and the physics of lightning
items.author: Google Gemini
items.summary: Each scene unfolds into interactive layers with guided explanations, from Silk Road trade routes to the inside of a jet engine.

items.title: Basecamp for Claude is live in the Claude directory
items.author: DHH
items.summary: DHH announced the Basecamp connector in Claude's directory, so project data is reachable from Claude.

items.title: Android MCP and AppFunctions API enter beta so apps can expose capabilities to agents
items.author: Android Developers
items.summary: Apps can share their capabilities with your own agent or system agents through the AppFunctions API.

items.title: Claude for Legal adds a gallery of ready-made artifacts for contract review and cite checks
items.author: Claude
items.summary: A built-in gallery covers contract review, regulatory horizon scans and cite checks that you can extend with your own documents and connectors and share across the business.

sections.title: Key Insights and Builder Wins
sections.description: Builders, creators and indie founders showing what they made and what happened.

items.title: Pieter Levels: Hotelist hits 700,000+ visitors a month, now adds invite-only profiles
items.author: @levelsio
items.summary: Levels says Hotelist, his site that shows real hotel ratings instead of inflated booking-site scores, is now his most popular property at over 700,000 monthly visitors. He added user profiles with invites today.
key_takeaways: 700,000+ monthly visitors, per the author.
Invite-only profiles are the next growth step.
suggested_actions: List one data set people distrust in your category and build the honest-rating version.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a small honest-data site can become a traffic machine. Try it: find a rating everyone suspects is inflated in your trade and publish the corrected one.

items.title: Pieter Levels' browser port of Quake 1 becomes a popular QuakeWorld server
items.author: @levelsio
items.summary: Levels' web port, started as a nostalgia project two years ago, now fills up daily with newcomers, and the QuakeWorld community asked him to add WebRTC and QTV so people can watch matches.
key_takeaways: A hobby port found a living community.
Players asked for WebRTC and QTV to spectate games.
suggested_actions: Ship a nostalgic web version of something you love and see who shows up.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a playful side project can attract a real community. Try it: put a classic you love in the browser this weekend and share the link with one forum.

items.title: Tony Dinh ships Vikey, a Vietnamese keyboard that auto-switches between English and Vietnamese at 99.73% accuracy
items.author: Tony Dinh
items.summary: Solo founder Tony Dinh built Vikey to end the manual language toggle he made about 300 times a day on laptop and phone, and reports 99.73% accuracy.
key_takeaways: Built to fix one annoyance the author felt personally.
Accuracy figure is the author's own.
suggested_actions: List the three small friction points you hit daily and pick one to build for.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: scratch your own repeated annoyance. Try it: track what irritates you for a week and have an agent prototype the fix.

items.title: Jack Friks relaunches an app after his last one reached 150,000 downloads and about 100 million social views
items.author: jack friks
items.summary: Friks says last year's app hit $5k a month within two months and 150,000 downloads, and he has remade it at a larger scale. His follow-up says fresh Instagram and TikTok accounts earned nearly 100,000,000 views without his own following.
key_takeaways: 150,000 downloads and $5k a month in two months, per the author.
Growth came from fresh social accounts, not an existing audience.
suggested_actions: Study how a new account can seed short-form views for a small product.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: short-form video as a launch engine for small apps. Try it: post five short demos of one tool from a brand-new account and track installs.

secondary_urls.label: Friks on 100M views from fresh accounts

items.title: Ethan Mollick had Opus build WONTFIX, a game that turns real JIRA tickets into horror-game audio logs
items.author: Ethan Mollick
items.summary: The playable demo takes tickets from any of your real projects and converts them into dramatic audio logs that form the plot of a 2000s-style horror game set on an abandoned space station. Code is on GitHub.
key_takeaways: Playable demo and open code are linked.
Any project's ticket history becomes story material.
suggested_actions: Feed your own backlog in and share the results with the team.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn dull work artifacts into entertainment. Try it: run last quarter's tickets through it and play the audio logs at the next team gathering.

items.title: Baoyu's 7-year-old now builds and edits games in ChatGPT by voice
items.author: 宝玉
items.summary: Baoyu (@dotey) writes, in Chinese, that his 7-year-old moved from drawing pictures to video to a playable game, then kept editing it by voice because he types poorly.
key_takeaways: Progression: images, then video, then a game that gets edited live.
Voice input removed the typing barrier.
suggested_actions: Let a child or a non-coder in your life try building a small game by voice.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: voice plus iteration lets anyone build. Try it: sit a colleague who never codes in front of ChatGPT and ask them to make a simple game about their job.

items.title: Alex Finn builds 5 dashboards with Grok Bot's new Pages feature, including one that saved usage
items.author: Alex Finn
items.summary: Finn says Grok Bot's biggest update yet adds pages and dashboards, and shows five dashboards that make it easier to use.
key_takeaways: Pages and dashboards give the agent a persistent surface.
One of the five dashboards cut his usage.
suggested_actions: Build a "daily status" page that your agent refreshes each morning.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give your agent a page it keeps current. Try it: ask an agent to build a one-page dashboard of your calendar, tasks and key numbers.
items.recurrence_note: Grok Bot builder stories ran last week (autonomous business, phone calls); this week covers the Pages and dashboards update.

items.title: Justine Moore let her Grok Bot pick and buy a gift with up to $100; it arrived with a Halloween surprise
items.author: Justine Moore
items.summary: She gave the agent access to up to $100 from her X Money account and asked it to use her tweets and conversations to choose. Elon Musk then announced that Grok Bot will research gifts for your friends and family and buy them.
key_takeaways: Budget cap of $100 set by the user; the agent chose and bought.
Musk says the feature extends to friends and family gifts.
suggested_actions: Ask an agent to shortlist three gifts from a person's public posts.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: delegate gift-picking to an agent that knows taste. Try it: give it the list and a budget before the next birthday.
items.recurrence_note: Grok Bot has appeared in recent weeks; this is the first purchase-on-your-behalf example.

items.title: Google DeepMind's PlanAssist cuts UK householder planning assessment time by up to 58% and expands to 12 more councils
items.author: Google DeepMind
items.summary: Built with Gemini, PlanAssist checks documents and drawings, heritage constraints and policy, and drafts cited assessment reports. In pilots at Barnet, Camden and Dorset it cut officer assessment time by up to 58%, and over 70% of reports needed no edits.
key_takeaways: Up to 58% less officer time in early pilots.
Over 70% of generated reports needed no edits.
Pilot grows to 15 councils; national availability planned for 2027, subject to testing.
suggested_actions: Look at where your own permitting or approval steps are checklist-heavy.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: an agent that pre-reads applications against rules and drafts a cited report. Try it: run it on a stack of past product-approval or spec-review packets.

secondary_urls.label: DeepMind: Speeding up planning decisions with AI

sections.title: AI for Science
sections.description: Drug design, instruments, papers and scientists adopting agents.

items.title: Anthropic expands AI for Science to 20 foundations, institutions and research groups with free Claude credits
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: The program now includes Sloan, Simons, Schmidt Sciences, NSF, Sanger Institute, Crick Institute, EMBL and others, covering neuroscience, climate, cancer, genomics, mathematics and rare disease. Work includes lab-instrument standards and AI-assisted data analysis.
key_takeaways: 20 named partners, free Claude credits, no amounts stated.
Includes lab-instrument standards, genomics and climate work.
suggested_actions: See whether a funder you work with is on the list and ask about credits.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: free-credit programs let researchers test agents on real data. Try it: apply for a science program and give one researcher a month of access.

items.title: Immunologist Derya Unutmaz uses Codex to simulate how a single cell responds to a drug
items.author: OpenAI Developers
items.summary: OpenAI Developers highlights Derya Unutmaz (@DeryaTR_) as one of nine builders in a Codex community sharing projects, with his use case simulating a single cell's drug response.
key_takeaways: A working immunologist, not an engineer, is the example.
Part of a set of nine Codex builder stories.
suggested_actions: Ask a biologist or chemist what simulation they have wanted but never coded.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: scientists describing an experiment and letting a coding agent simulate it. Try it: have a researcher describe a simple model in words and ask Codex for a first runnable version.

items.title: Tanishq Abraham: Claude Opus 5.5 one-shotted an explainer video that made a Meta paper understandable
items.author: Tanishq Mathew Abraham, Ph.D.
items.summary: He asked Opus 5.5 to produce an explainer video for Meta's patch-level self-supervised learning paper (JEM) and says after watching he had a decent grasp of how it works.
key_takeaways: One prompt produced a paper explainer video.
Author says it left him understanding the method.
suggested_actions: Ask an agent to make a 3-minute explainer for the paper on your desk.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn dense papers into short videos. Try it: pick this week's must-read in your field and share the video with your group instead of the PDF.

items.title: alphaXiv launches NotebookLM for arXiv papers: conversational audio drawn from thousands of related papers
items.author: alphaXiv
items.summary: The feature turns dense AI research into spoken conversations, with context from related work that draws connections to the state of the art.

items.title: alphaXiv autoarxiv: swap "arxiv" for "autoarxiv" in any paper URL to run a minimal reproduction
items.author: alphaXiv
items.summary: OpenResearch sets up an environment on your compute, runs a minimal reproduction, tracks logs, visualizes runs and produces artifacts in a closed local loop.

items.title: NVIDIA: SimBioSys' FDA-cleared TumorSight Risk estimates five- and ten-year breast cancer recurrence risk before surgery
items.author: NVIDIA
items.summary: The tool analyzes an existing breast MRI with pathology and clinical information for patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative early-stage disease.

sections.title: Viral Breakouts
sections.description: High-engagement posts surfaced by the viral sweep from accounts outside the curated list.

items.title: Thariq: technical people are sad their skills seem useless while non-technical people wish they were more technical
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Thariq (Anthropic) observes that agents have flipped the mood: engineers fear their skills are obsolete, while non-technical people want technical skill to steer agents better. The post drew 36,946 likes and 1.9 million views.
key_takeaways: Agent use rewards technical judgment, which non-technical users now actively want.
The demand signal sits with people who have domain expertise but no coding background.
suggested_actions: Offer a two-hour agent workshop to your domain experts, not just engineers.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: your scientists are the non-technical people wishing they could steer agents. Try it: pair a researcher with an agent on their own dataset for an afternoon and let them drive.

items.title: Thariq builds an AI-native macOS dock with writing and building modes that classifies your activity in real time
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Thariq's personal project is a dock with custom modes that help him stay focused. The agent customizes mode behavior itself and uses jev to classify his activity and notifications as they happen. It drew 10,105 likes.
key_takeaways: Modes are editable by the agent, so the tool reshapes itself around your day.
Real-time classification of activity and notifications drives the behavior.
suggested_actions: Define two modes you would want on your own desktop and ask an agent to draft the dock.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a desktop that changes shape with the task. Try it: ask an agent to build a menu-bar tool with a "deep work" mode that silences everything except the three apps you name.

items.title: Codex lead Tibo: ChatGPT now switches between multiple accounts on mobile, desktop next
items.author: Tibo
items.summary: Tibo Sottiaux (@thsottiaux) posted Day 26 of his daily-drop series: multiple ChatGPT accounts on mobile now, desktop coming, plus two usage resets banked. The post reached 3.0 million views and 14,419 likes.
key_takeaways: Mobile account switching is live; desktop is coming soon.
Reset days are part of an ongoing series of drops.
suggested_actions: Link a work and a personal account on your phone and try switching mid-task.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a daily-drop cadence builds a following. Try it: ship one small improvement every day for 30 days and post each one.

items.title: Poteto Playground goes viral: tap potatoes and the lucky one sends you to ChatGPT
items.author: Tibo
items.summary: Tibo Sottiaux's post of poteto.com reached 5.0 million views and 12,765 likes; he later noted the site passed 3 million views. The page is a potato playground where tapping reveals secret notes and the lucky potato triggers a trip to ChatGPT.
key_takeaways: A tiny playful site drew millions of views.
The page promises a trip to ChatGPT from the lucky potato.
suggested_actions: Build a one-screen toy that points to your product.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a toy page is a marketing channel. Try it: have an agent build a one-page game for your next launch.

items.title: Google's TPUs phoned home from orbit: four chips ran a prompt in space
items.author: Google
items.summary: In early October Google sent four TPUs into orbit to see whether they could turn on, process a prompt and transmit a response; Google says this week it got its answer.

items.title: DeepMind agents on Gemini 4 Argon and Antigravity build a dancing 12-degree-of-freedom pumpkin robot from one prompt
items.author: Google
items.summary: Google says the team used AI agents to bring a physical robot to life from scratch. A teammate's post says it came from a single plain-English prompt.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: describe a physical gadget and let agents design it. Try it: ask a coding agent to design a simple desk toy from a sentence.

items.title: Artificial Analysis gives GPT-6.1 Sol a robot arm and a pen, and it writes "the three scariest words in AI"
items.author: Artificial Analysis
items.summary: AA-Robotics published a Halloween test where a model controls a robot arm to write by hand; a related AA post shows another model dabbing "hello world" dot by dot in 3,270 arm moves.

items.title: Guillermo Rauch shares sf-blimp.vercel.app: fly over San Francisco
items.author: Guillermo Rauch
items.summary: The page loads as "SF Blimp - Fly Over San Francisco," a playful interactive demo from the Vercel CEO.

items.title: Thariq adds a fire-fighting taekwondo master to his AI-assisted side-project game, now with generated sprites
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Thariq says the art style moved from 3D models to generated sprites. His earlier post argues to use AI to bring your vision to life rather than outsource the creative process.

items.title: Ethan Mollick: Genie 4 runs DOOM, with an office where every wall is DOOM and a demon coworker gives you a bonus
items.author: Ethan Mollick
items.summary: Mollick shared a Genie 4 scene prompt in which everything in a typical office is DOOM, down to his demon coworker with a chaingun who gives him a bonus.

sections.title: Hot Takes and Debates
sections.description: Two substantive disagreements with a clear position on each side.

items.title: Position: Google "cooked" with Argon 4
items.author: ThePrimeagen
items.summary: ThePrimeagen says Google cooked with Argon 4.
items.why_it_matters: Opposite call to theo's test of Argon 4 on real code bases.

items.title: Counter: Argon 4 hallucinates badly in a real codebase, "10x worse"
items.author: Theo - t3.gg
items.summary: Theo replies that the model cannot work in a real code base without egregious hallucination, and calls it ten times worse, not 5%.
items.why_it_matters: Opposite call to ThePrimeagen on Argon 4.

items.title: Position: SaaS is becoming free; charge for the agent that does the work
items.author: GREG ISENBERG
items.summary: Greg Isenberg: give away the CRM, dashboard and app, and charge for the agent that does the work.
items.why_it_matters: Opposite emphasis to Jon Yongfook's view that narrow tools for a tech audience on X are what is dead.

items.title: Counter: SaaS is not dead; narrow software for a tech audience on X is
items.author: Jon Yongfook
items.summary: Jon Yongfook says SaaS is not dead, but narrowly scoped software you can easily sell to a tech audience on X is.
items.why_it_matters: Opposite emphasis to Greg Isenberg's "SaaS is free" view.

emerging_signals.pattern: One folder, one agent, one finished artifact
emerging_signals.evidence: Levels' Claude Code vlog edit (https://x.com/levelsio/status/2116959423117857026), Karpathy's HackerTube (https://x.com/karpathy/status/2116957135661945283) and Mollick's WONTFIX game (https://x.com/emollick/status/2115981377652822479) all came from a coding agent working in a folder.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether non-coders start reporting the same folder-based workflow for reports and decks.

emerging_signals.evidence: ChatGPT Dot texting (https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2115496387613786374), Grok Bot Pages and gift buying (https://x.com/venturetwins/status/2116643253726683590), Hermes mobile beta (https://x.com/testingcatalog/status/2116590276076580979) and Perplexity voice (https://x.com/AravSrinivas/status/2115476775505658135).
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Which agent first combines texting, voice and purchases in one flow.

emerging_signals.pattern: Agents drive scientific instruments and lab workflows
emerging_signals.evidence: Allen Telescope Array agents (https://x.com/NVIDIAAI/status/2116560120457142451), Anthropic drug-development partners (https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2115178675050307942) and a Codex single-cell simulation (https://x.com/OpenAIDevs/status/2115854891650523391).
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Instrument vendors exposing command interfaces for agents.

emerging_signals.pattern: Open weights close on the frontier and fit on desktops
emerging_signals.evidence: Mistral Large 4 weights (https://x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2115820547103952925), Unsloth 1-bit on a Mac Studio (https://x.com/UnslothAI/status/2115812784189620265), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash GGUFs (https://x.com/cursor_ai/status/2114839997568405608).
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Qwen 4 next week, per Kimmonismus citing Qwen code (rumor; https://x.com/kimmonismus/status/2116648154829656300).

emerging_signals.pattern: Rumor-labeled: next Anthropic and OpenAI models
emerging_signals.evidence: Kimmonismus and TestingCatalog say a "Claude Mythos 5.5" mention appeared in the HTML of Anthropic's website (https://x.com/testingcatalog/status/2116915996850074008), and Kimmonismus says GPT-6.2 appears in Codex usage analytics (https://x.com/kimmonismus/status/2116845494454350227). Neither is confirmed by the labs.

emerging_signals.pattern: Google folds Jules into Antigravity and adds a plugin marketplace
emerging_signals.evidence: TestingCatalog reports Google is shutting down Jules and moving features into Antigravity (https://x.com/testingcatalog/status/2115960927275368958), and that Antigravity launched a Plugins marketplace with Jira, Notion, Stripe and Linear connectors (https://x.com/testingcatalog/status/2115889458935382213).
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Cloud execution support in Antigravity next week, per TestingCatalog.

suggested_refinements.notes: Access: X search and a logged-in timeline were not available. Posts were gathered from api.fxtwitter.com profile timelines for about 140 handles (each returns a mix of the account's notable posts and related posts, not a full chronological feed), so the viral sweep covers handles queried and posts surfaced in those timelines. Window used: Oct 26 00:00 ET to Nov 1 23:59 ET. Every item was refetched at build time for text, date and counts. Linked pages read for the Top Picks: hackertube.org, Anthropic's drug-development and AI for Science posts, NVIDIA's telescope post and DeepMind's PlanAssist post. Terra, Genie 4, Dot texting and Canva Brush rest on the posting company's own account. Gaps: @xai and @xAI returned server errors; @windsurf_ai, @bolt_new, @GroqInc and @lmarena_ai returned no posts; several handles (@LangChainAI, @lovable_dev, @elevenlabsio) returned 404 and may have changed. @karpathy posted once in the window and is a Top Pick. Materials-science and building-science posts were thin on X this week; the building-related item is DeepMind's PlanAssist. Engagement counts rise after fetch. Freshness: no post repeats last week's edition; 3 of 61 items continue a theme from last week and are tagged returning_theme.
